title: No spec text on when receiveTypingIndicators=false takes effect on open connections
description:
Chat.receiveTypingIndicators can be changed via Chat/set while a WebSocket connection is open and a ChatStreamEnable subscription is active. The spec requires checking at delivery time (correct for correctness), but does not address the latency window between the Chat/set call completing and the server's delivery path observing the new value.

In a distributed deployment (multiple WebSocket nodes behind a load balancer), a Chat/set write may propagate to the delivery path with a delay. The spec is silent on:
- Whether the new value must take effect immediately (within the same request/response cycle) or at best-effort
- Whether any in-flight typing events already queued before the field change should be suppressed or allowed through

This creates a spec maintenance headache: implementers will make different choices, and the spec provides no normative baseline to test conformance against. The spec should add a sentence: 'The updated value of receiveTypingIndicators MUST be used for events delivered after the Chat/set response is returned to the client. Events already queued for delivery before the Chat/set call completes MAY be delivered under the prior setting.'

Relevant locations: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md Chat/set Updating a Chat section; draft-atwood-jmap-chat-wss-00.md Section 6 Security ephemeral event authorization.
